verdicts.note: Attacked toward 0. He holds several in-office roles (field training officer, armorer, search and rescue coordinator, union president; S1), and his grandfather was sheriff (S1, S2). Still, he has about four years as a deputy (since 2022, S1) and is seeking the top job over the seven-year undersheriff. His platform centers on recruiting and retention changes (S1), so +1 at medium is fair. S1 is in his frontmatter. Display defect: the third highlight says he 'Calls retaining qualified deputies the office's biggest challenge'. His dossier quotes him calling it 'one of the biggest challenges' (S1), and the highlight should say 'one of the biggest challenges'. _contest.md has the same overstatement ('the office's biggest challenge'). The other highlights and the summary match S1 and S3. Race blurb: the facts match _contest.md (open seat, S1; 533 to 415, S3; four deputies resigned while a hiring freeze was in place, S5 and S6). 'Resigned ... under a county hiring freeze' could be read as claiming a cause. The dossier records only that both happened, so 'during a county hiring freeze' would be more neutral.

Attacked on confidence. He runs explicitly on 'the leadership, knowledge, and commitment' of 17 years in law enforcement, seven as undersheriff, plus 11 years in management (S1), and the newspaper profile repeats it (S2). He is the office's second-in-command, not the incumbent sheriff, so -1 rather than -2. High confidence is supported by two sources with an explicit record-based pitch. S1 and S2 are in his frontmatter. Display: the summary and highlights match the dossier (undersheriff seven years, 17 years, jail commander, S1 and S2; 11 years in management, S1; the 'public safety begins with strong relationships' quote, S1; 415 to 533, S3). No safety scores are proposed for either candidate. Neither dossier states an enforcement or prevention agenda, as _contest.md notes.
